Short Description: This test checks the value of the UTL_FILE_DIR parameter.  The UTL_FILE package allows host file access from within the database using the permissions and privileges assigned to the Oracle database process or service.  This package should be used with caution.  All files accessible to using this package are equally accessible to any database user with execute permissions to the UTL_FILE package.  When UTL_FILE_DIR is set to '*', then all directories accessible to the Oracle database process, typically the Oracle installation account, are accessible via the UTL_FILE package This setting effectively turns off directory access checking, and makes any directory accessible to the UTL_FILE functions. The UTL_FILE_DIR list should specify only authorized and protected directories and should not include only fully specified path names.
SQL: SELECT COUNT (*)     FROM V$PARAMETER    WHERE      UPPER (VALUE) LIKE '%*%'          AND UPPER (NAME) = 'UTL_FILE_DIR'
SQL For Details: SELECT  'PARAMETER NAME: '||NAME ||'   VALUE : '||VALUE     FROM V$PARAMETER    WHERE UPPER (NAME)= 'UTL_FILE_DIR'
Result Text Fail: The  UTL_FILE_DIR parameter value is  not  acceptable. The parameter must not contain *
Result Text Pass: The UTL_FILE_DIR  parameter value is acceptable

Short Description: This test checks the value of the GLOBAL_NAMES parameter.  The GLOBAL_NAMES parameter specifies the requirement to use the full Oracle global name in order to reference it in a database link.  Requiring the full global name protects remote database from inadvertent access. CIS Oracle Database 2.2.3
SQL: SELECT count(*)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='GLOBAL_NAMES' and UPPER(VALUE) ='TRUE'
SQL For Details: SELECT UPPER(VALUE)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='GLOBAL_NAMES'

Result Text Pass: The GLOBAL_NAMES parameter value is acceptable

Short Description: This test checks the value of the O7_DICTIONARY_ACCESSIBILITY parameter.  Oracle 8 provides the parameter O7_DICTIONARY_ACCESSIBILITY to prevent accounts with the privilege SELECT ANY TABLE from selecting the data dictionary tables. Setting this parameter to FALSE helps restrict access to sensitive data in the data dictionary such as the encrypted passwords.    CIS 2.2.10

Short Description: This test checks the value of the REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT parameter.  Setting this value to TRUE allows operating system authentication over an insecure connection. Trusting remote operating systems can allow a user to impersonate another operating system user and connect to the database without having to supply a password. If REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT is set to true, the only information a remote user needs to connect to the database is the name of any user whose account is setup to be authenticated by the operating system.    CIS 2.2.8
SQL: SELECT count(*)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT' and UPPER(VALUE) ='FALSE'
SQL For Details: SELECT UPPER(VALUE)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT'
Result Text Fail: The REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT  parameter value is  not  acceptable. The parameter must be FALSE
Result Text Pass: The REMOTE_OS_AUTHENT parameter value is acceptable

Short Description: This test checks the value of the REMOTE_OS_ROLES parameter.  Setting REMOTE_OS_ROLES to TRUE allows operating system groups to control Oracle roles. The default value of FALSE causes roles to be identified and managed by the database. If REMOTE_OS_ROLE is set to TRUE, a remote user could impersonate another operating system user over a network connection. It is a security risk to use operating system role authentication for network clients.   CIS 2.2.9
SQL: SELECT count(*)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='REMOTE_OS_ROLES' and UPPER(VALUE) ='FALSE'
SQL For Details: SELECT UPPER(VALUE)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='REMOTE_OS_ROLES'
Result Text Fail: The REMOTE_OS_ROLES  parameter value is  not  acceptable. The parameter must be FALSE
Result Text Pass: The REMOTE_OS_ROLES parameter value is acceptable

Short Description: This test checks the value of the _TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC parameter.  The _TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC parameter is used to make trace files used for debugging database applications and events available to all database users. Use of this capability precludes the discrete assignment of privileges based on job function.  Additionally, its use may provide access to external files and data to unauthorized users. The value for the _TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC parameter by default is false when it is not set.   If the parameter does not exist or is set to FALSE, this is not a finding.      CIS 2.2.17
SQL: select sum(a) from    ( SELECT count(*) a   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME) = '_TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC'    union all   SELECT count(*) a   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='_TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC' and value='FALSE')
SQL For Details: SELECT UPPER(VALUE)   FROM V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER   WHERE UPPER(NAME)='_TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC'

Result Text Pass: The _TRACE_FILES_PUBLIC parameter value is acceptable

Short Description: This test checks the value of the PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION parameter for all profiles.  The PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION value specifies a PL/SQL function to be used for password verification when users who are assigned this profile login to a database. This function can be used to validate password strength by requiring passwords to pass a strength test written in PL/SQL. The function must be locally available for execution on the database to which this profile applies. Oracle provides a default script (utlpwdmg.sql), but you can also create your own function. The password verification function must be owned by SYS. The default setting for this profile parameter is NULL, meaning no password verification is performed.   CIS Oracle Database 3.8
SQL: SELECT count(*)   FROM DBA_PROFILES   WHERE RESOURCE_NAME='PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION'   AND (LIMIT = 'DEFAULT' OR LIMIT = 'NULL' OR LIMIT is NULL)
SQL For Details: SELECT 'Profile: '||PROFILE||' Resource Name: '||RESOURCE_NAME   FROM DBA_PROFILES   WHERE RESOURCE_NAME='PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION'   AND (LIMIT = 'DEFAULT' OR LIMIT = 'NULL'   OR LIMIT is NULL )
Result Text Fail: The PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION parameter is  not correctly set
Result Text Pass: The PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION parameter is correctly set for all profiles

Short Description: SEC_MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS specifies the number of authentication attempts that can be made by a client on a connection to the server process.  After the specified number of failure attempts, the connection will be automatically dropped by the server process.  An unlimited number of login attempts for a user connection can facilitate both brute-force login attacks and the occurrence of Denial-of-Service.  The SEC_MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS parameter should be set between 1 to 3 according to the STIG and CIS recommendations.  The Guardium recommended default threshold is 3.  The threshold can be adjusted to a higher or lower value to accommodate your organizational needs.   CIS Oracle Database   2.2.12

Result Text Fail: The SEC_MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS  parameter value is  not  acceptable. The parameter must be  3 or less
Result Text Pass: The SEC_MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS parameter value is acceptable

Short Description: Undetected attacks using bad packets can lead to a successful Denial of Service (DoS) to database clients. Short Description: Production databases should be protected from unauthorized access by developers on shared production/development host systems. Developers granted elevated database, operating system privileges on systems that support both development, and production databases can affect the operation and/or security of the production database system. This test excludes grantees from a predefined Guardium group called "Oracle exclude default system grantees" and APEX_.  This test also excludes grantees that are ANONYMOUS and PUBLIC. Short Description: The remote admin connections option controls whether a client application on a remote   computer can use the Dedicated Administrator Connection (DAC).The Dedicated Administrator Connection (DAC) lets an administrator access a running   server to execute diagnostic functions or Transact-SQL statements, or to troubleshoot   problems on the server, even when the server is locked or running in an abnormal state   and not responding to a SQL Server Database Engine connection. In a cluster scenario, the   administrator may not actually be logged on to the same node that is currently hosting the   SQL Server instance and thus is considered "remote". Therefore, this setting should usually   be enabled (1) for SQL Server failover clusters; otherwise it should be disabled (0) which is   the default.

Short Description: public is a special fixed server role containing all logins. Unlike other fixed server roles,   permissions can be changed for the public role. Test Description: AA_SqlServer_330_Revoke public login from SQL Server agent proxy account
Short Description: The public database role contains every user in the msdb database. SQL Agent proxies   define a security context in which a job step can run.Granting access to SQL Agent proxies for the public role would allow all users to utilize the proxy which may have high privileges. This would likely break the principle of least   privileges.
SQL: SELECT count(*)   FROM msdb.dbo.sysproxylogin spl   JOIN sys.database_principals dp   ON dp.sid = spl.sid   JOIN msdb.dbo.sysproxies sp   ON sp.proxy_id = spl.proxy_id   WHERE principal_id = USER_ID('public')
SQL For Details: SELECT 'proxyname : '+CAST(sp.name  as varchar)   FROM msdb.dbo.sysproxylogin spl   JOIN sys.database_principals dp   ON dp.sid = spl.sid   JOIN msdb.dbo.sysproxies sp   ON sp.proxy_id = spl.proxy_id   WHERE principal_id = USER_ID('public')
Result Text Fail: There are some public permissions on SQL Server agent proxy account
Result Text Pass: There are no public permissions on SQL Server agent proxy account
